mainEntity.name: Can a Robotic Case Packer Handle Yogurt Cups and Tubs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. TRFRapidpack handles cups and tubs, and TRFOnepack handles cups. Cup geometry, lid type and case format decide how the package is gripped, placed and protected, so TRF defines the end-of-arm tool and pack pattern with real packages before the design of your dairy case packing line is fixed.

mainEntity.name: Can a Conveyor System Be Designed for Both Dry and Washdown Zones in the Same Plant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. TRFCleanflow has a Dry line for dry and low-moisture zones and a Washdown line for frequent washdown. TRF engineers the transition between zones so the hygienic section ends where the sanitation requirement ends, and TRFIntraflow takes over once product is in a case.

mainEntity.name: Can a Robotic Palletizer Operate Below Freezing (32°F)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, with equipment built for it. When the palletizing area runs below 32°F, as in frozen dairy production, the TRF line points to TRFSubzero. For any other cold room, TRF engineering confirms the platform during the application review. Ice cream has its own page: frozen food and ice cream.

mainEntity.name: How Do You Choose Between TRFCobot, TRFCompact and TRFSpeed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose by line speed, case weight and floor space: TRFCobot fits smaller dairy lines that still stack pallets by hand and change patterns often. TRFCompact adds industrial duty cycle in a packaging room where floor space is scarce. TRFSpeed fits high-volume plants that consolidate several lines into one palletizing area. TRF validates the choice with your real cases and pallet patterns.

mainEntity.name: Can One Automation Partner Supply Palletizing, Case Packing and Conveyors for a Dairy Plant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. TRF supplies cheese packaging automation and dairy packaging automation as one integrated solution: TRFCleanflow carries exposed product, TRFRapidpack, TRFOnepack or TRFDroppack pack the cases, TRFIntraflow moves them, and TRFCobot, TRFCompact or TRFSpeed build the pallet. One partner is responsible from layout to startup, and Parts and Service supports TRF-supplied equipment afterward.

mainEntity.name: How Is Payback Estimated for Dairy Packaging Automation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Payback depends on the labor hours the system replaces, shifts per day, local labor cost and the installed cost of the system. The estimate divides the system cost, including maintenance, by the annual net savings: the labor cost of manual palletizing minus the electricity the robot uses. The palletizing ROI calculator applies this method to your location, your shifts and the people who palletize by hand today.
